steps: Compare the platform chooser of the admin account with what the Supplier and Subcontractor accounts see.
expected: The admin account sees 'Voyage Control Admin'; the Supplier and Subcontractor accounts do not.
PM-REG-ROLE-11.actual: As expected. The Supplier and Subcontractor accounts have access to one platform only and were shown no platform chooser.

PM-REG-ROLE-12.title: Role given when inviting a user
PM-REG-ROLE-12.description: Checks that a user invited from SCP with the Supplier role gets exactly the Supplier role's access.
steps: In SCP User Management, invite a test user with role 'Supplier', accept the invitation from the mailbox and log in.
expected: The new user has the Supplier role and exactly that role's access.
PM-REG-ROLE-12.actual: Not run: accepting the invitation needs the test mailbox, which shows a 'verify you are human' check to automation.
PM-REG-ROLE-12.needed: A mailbox the automation can read without a human check, or another way to activate an invited user.

PM-REG-ROLE-13.title: Organisation admin creates a user in the portal
PM-REG-ROLE-13.description: Checks that the organisation admin can create a user with a role in the admin portal and that the user can then log in with that access.
steps: In Voyage Control Admin > 'Supply Chain Planner', create a test user with role 'Subcontractor'.
expected: The user is created with that role and can log in to SCP with Subcontractor access.
PM-REG-ROLE-13.actual: Not run: creating a user changes the shared admin portal and is waiting for approval.
PM-REG-ROLE-13.needed: Approval to create a user, and a mailbox the automation can use to activate the new user.

PM-REG-ROLE-14.title: Non-admin users cannot reach role administration
PM-REG-ROLE-14.description: Checks that Supplier and Subcontractor users cannot open the role administration in the admin portal.
steps: As the Supplier account, look for the 'Voyage Control Admin' entry and try to open the admin portal's Roles page.
As the Subcontractor account, look for the 'Voyage Control Admin' entry and try to open the admin portal's Roles page.
expected: There is no 'Voyage Control Admin' entry and the Roles page is not available.
There is no 'Voyage Control Admin' entry and the Roles page is not available.
PM-REG-ROLE-14.actual: As expected. Both accounts were sent to the sign-in page instead.

PM-REG-ROLE-15.title: 'New message' follows System Messages permission
PM-REG-ROLE-15.description: Checks that the 'New message' button on System Messages is offered only to roles allowed to create messages.
steps: As the Supplier account, open System Messages by its web address.
As the Subcontractor account, open System Messages by its web address.
expected: The page is usable only with Project Management tab access, and 'New message' only with a create permission.
The page is usable only with Project Management tab access, and 'New message' only with a create permission.
PM-REG-ROLE-15.actual: As expected. System Messages could not be used by either account, so 'New message' was not reached.

PM-REG-ROLE-16.title: Deleting System Messages follows the permission
PM-REG-ROLE-16.description: Checks that only roles with the 'System Messages: Delete' permission are offered a way to delete a message.
steps: Read 'System Messages: Delete (Project)' on the Project Admin role without saving, then open System Messages as Project Admin.
As the Supplier account, try to reach a 'Delete' action on System Messages.
As the Subcontractor account, try to reach a 'Delete' action on System Messages.
expected: 'Delete' is offered only when the permission is enabled.
There is no way to delete a message, because the permission is not enabled.
There is no way to delete a message, because the permission is not enabled.
PM-REG-ROLE-16.actual: As expected. The Project Admin has the permission and was offered 'Delete'; for the Supplier and Subcontractor the page could not be used and no 'Delete' was offered.

PM-REG-ROLE-17.title: Watched Materials follows Material Watch permission
PM-REG-ROLE-17.description: Checks that the Watched Materials page is usable only by roles with the 'Users: Material Watch' permission.
steps: As the Supplier account, open Watched Materials by its web address.
As the Subcontractor account, open Watched Materials by its web address.
expected: The page is usable only when the role allows it.
The page is usable only when the role allows it.
PM-REG-ROLE-17.actual: As expected. The page could not be used by the Supplier account and opened for the Subcontractor account.

PM-REG-ROLE-18.title: Scope of a new System Message
PM-REG-ROLE-18.description: Checks whether a new System Message can be created for the whole platform or only the project, depending on the role.
steps: Check whether any test account's role may create System Messages.
expected: Where a role may create messages, the scope offered matches its permission.
PM-REG-ROLE-18.actual: As expected. No test account's role may create System Messages, so the scope was not checked.

PM-REG-ROLE-19.title: 'Add Rule' follows Inventory Control permission
PM-REG-ROLE-19.description: Checks that the 'Add Rule' button on Inventory Control is shown only to roles allowed to add control rules.
steps: As the Supplier account, open Inventory Control by its web address.
As the Subcontractor account, open Inventory Control by its web address.
expected: 'Add Rule' is shown only when the role allows adding control rules.
'Add Rule' is shown only when the role allows adding control rules.
PM-REG-ROLE-19.actual: As expected. The Supplier account saw 'Add Rule' (allowed); the Subcontractor account did not (not allowed).

PM-REG-ROLE-20.title: 'Assign' inspector follows the permission
PM-REG-ROLE-20.description: Checks that the 'Assign' action on First Delivery Inspections is shown only to roles with 'FDI: Assign Inspector'.
steps: Read 'FDI: Assign Inspector' on the Project Admin role without saving, then open First Delivery Inspections as Project Admin.
expected: 'Assign' is shown only when the permission is enabled.
PM-REG-ROLE-20.actual: As expected. The permission is enabled and 'Assign' was shown.

PM-REG-ROLE-21.title: Project Management access opens unprotected pages
PM-REG-ROLE-21.description: Checks that a role with Project Management tab access can open the Project Management pages that have no permission of their own.
steps: Check whether any test account's role has Project Management tab access.
expected: Where a role has that access, the pages without their own permission open.
PM-REG-ROLE-21.actual: As expected. No test account's role has Project Management tab access, so there was nothing to check.

PM-REG-ROLE-22.title: Organisation admin creates a project
PM-REG-ROLE-22.description: Checks that the organisation admin can create a new project in the admin portal.
steps: In Voyage Control Admin, click 'New Project', enter a test project name, the first Region, an address and the admin account as Project Owner, and click 'Create Project'.
expected: The project is listed under Projects.
PM-REG-ROLE-22.actual: As expected. Region us-west-2 was used; no message was shown.

PM-REG-ROLE-23.title: Project Admin limited to own organisation
PM-REG-ROLE-23.description: Checks that a Project Admin creating a project can choose only their own organisation.
steps: As a Project Admin, open project creation and look at the organisation list.
expected: Only the Project Admin's own organisation is offered.
PM-REG-ROLE-23.actual: Not run: there is no account that is only a Project Admin; the available Project Admin account is a platform admin.
PM-REG-ROLE-23.needed: An account that is only a Project Admin.

PM-REG-ROLE-24.title: Projects are created only in the admin portal
PM-REG-ROLE-24.description: Checks that projects can be created only in the Voyage Control Admin portal and that other users have no way to create one.
steps: As the organisation admin, open Voyage Control Admin.
As Project Admin in SCP, look for a create-project control on the dashboard, the menu and the project selector.
As the Supplier account, look for a create-project control in SCP and try the admin portal's projects page.
As the Subcontractor account, look for a create-project control in SCP and try the admin portal's projects page.
expected: 'New Project' is shown.
There is no create-project control in SCP.
There is no create-project control and the admin portal's projects page is not available.
There is no create-project control and the admin portal's projects page is not available.
PM-REG-ROLE-24.actual: As expected. Note: the Supplier role has 'Project: Create a new project' enabled, but there is no place where this user could create a project; this is an open question for the team.

PM-REG-SITE-01.title: Site and location type choices
PM-REG-SITE-01.description: Checks that the Add Site and Add Location forms offer the expected site and location types.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click 'Add Site', open the 'Choose Site' dropdown, then close the form.
Click 'ADD' on the first site row, open the 'Choose Location' dropdown, then close the form.
expected: The page opens.
The choices are 'Warehouse', 'Site_type3' and 'Site'.
The choices are 'Construction Area' and 'Substore'.

PM-REG-SITE-02.title: Site row menu actions
PM-REG-SITE-02.description: Checks that each site row offers Edit and Delete actions.
steps: On Site Details, click the menu icon of the first site, then close the menu.
expected: The menu shows 'Edit' and 'Delete'.

PM-REG-SITE-03.title: Add Site requires type and name
PM-REG-SITE-03.description: Checks that a site cannot be added without a site type and a name.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click 'Add Site' and submit the form with nothing filled in.
Submit it with no site type.
Submit it with no name.
expected: The page opens.
The form stays open and nothing is added.
The form stays open and nothing is added.
The form stays open and nothing is added.
PM-REG-SITE-03.actual: As expected. No message was shown in any of the attempts.

PM-REG-SITE-04.title: Add a site
PM-REG-SITE-04.description: Checks that a user can add a site and then choose it in the site selector at the top of the page.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click 'Add Site', choose site type 'Site', enter a test name, city 'Chennai' and country India (or the first listed), and click 'Add'.
Check the sites table, then reload and open the site selector in the page header.
expected: The page opens.
The form closes.
The new site is listed once and is offered in the site selector.

PM-REG-SITE-05.title: Add a location to a site
PM-REG-SITE-05.description: Checks that a user can add a location to a site.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click the location 'ADD' button on the test site, choose location type 'Construction Area', enter a test name and click 'Add'.
expected: The page opens.
The form closes and the site's location count goes up by 1.

PM-REG-SITE-06.title: Typing an address on Add Site
PM-REG-SITE-06.description: Checks how the address field on the Add Site form behaves when an address is typed, and that cancelling adds nothing.
steps: On Site Details, click 'Add Site' and type 'Anna Salai Chennai' in 'Start typing an address…'.
Close the form with Cancel or X.
expected: No suggestion list appears and the typed text stays in the field.
The form closes and nothing is added.

PM-REG-SITE-07.title: Site with deliveries cannot be deleted
PM-REG-SITE-07.description: Checks that a site that has already received deliveries cannot be deleted, so its delivery and stock history is kept.
steps: On Site Details, find a test site that has received deliveries in test runs.
Click 'Delete' in its row actions, confirm if asked, then reload the page.
expected: The site is listed.
The delete is refused or a warning is shown, and the site is still listed after reloading.
PM-REG-SITE-07.actual: After the general 'Are you sure you want to proceed?' prompt, the application showed 'Site deleted successfully!' and the site was removed, even though it had deliveries. Recorded as defect SCP-DEF-081.

PM-REG-SITE-09.title: Duplicate site name is refused
PM-REG-SITE-09.description: Checks that a site name already in use cannot be added again in different capital letters.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click 'Add Site', enter the test site's name in lower case, type 'Site' and city 'Chennai', and click 'Add'.
expected: The page opens.
Still only one site has this name.
PM-REG-SITE-09.actual: As expected. The form stayed open, with no message.

PM-REG-SITE-10.title: Duplicate location name in a site
PM-REG-SITE-10.description: Checks that a location name already used in a site cannot be added to it again.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Site Details'.
Click 'ADD' on the test site, enter the existing test location name with type 'Construction Area', and click 'Add'.
expected: The page opens.
The site's location count is unchanged.
PM-REG-SITE-10.actual: As expected. The form closed with no message and no extra location was added.

PM-REG-SITE-11.title: Export sites to Excel
PM-REG-SITE-11.description: Checks that exporting Site Details gives an Excel file listing the same sites as the page.
steps: On Site Details, click 'Export'.
expected: An Excel file downloads listing as many different site names as the page shows.
PM-REG-SITE-11.actual: The page listed 104 sites but the export had 120 rows covering only 91 different sites. It also included a location from another project, and the Location Type column showed an internal ID instead of a name in every row. Recorded as defect SCP-DEF-071.

PM-REG-SUB-01.title: Submittal Manager shows only a notice
PM-REG-SUB-01.description: Checks that the Submittal Manager page only shows a notice that it is being repurposed, with no working table or buttons.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Submittal Manager'.
Look at the page content.
expected: The page opens.
Only the notice 'This page is being repurposed.' is shown, with no table and no buttons.

PM-REG-SYS-00.title: No banners left over from earlier test runs
PM-REG-SYS-00.description: Checks that no active test banner from earlier automated runs is still shown to users.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
For every active test message left by earlier runs click 'Edit', untick 'Active' and 'Save', then reload.
expected: The page opens.
No test banner is shown.
PM-REG-SYS-00.actual: As expected. There were no leftover messages to switch off.

PM-REG-SYS-01.title: New system message form fields and limits
PM-REG-SYS-01.description: Checks that the form for a new system message offers the right scope, severity, length limits and date fields.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Note the first message, then click 'New message' (do not click 'Create').
Check the Scope, Severity, length limits and date fields.
expected: The page opens.
The form opens with a 'Create' button.

Scope offers 'Platform (all projects)' and 'Project (this project only)'; Severity offers Info and Warning; the title allows up to 120 characters; the body is required, allows up to 2000 characters and shows '0/2000'; there are two date-and-time fields and an 'Active' option.

PM-REG-SYS-02.title: Message preview shows formatting safely
PM-REG-SYS-02.description: Checks that the message preview shows bold, italic and link formatting, and does not show headings or run any script typed into the body.
steps: In the new message form type bold text, italic text and a link into the body.
Type a script tag and a heading line into the body.
expected: The preview shows the bold text, the italic text and a working link.
The preview shows no script and no heading, and the script does not run.

PM-REG-SYS-03.title: System message needs a body
PM-REG-SYS-03.description: Checks that a system message cannot be created without a body.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Click 'New message', enter a title but no body, then click 'Cancel'.
expected: The page opens.
The 'Create' button stays disabled.

PM-REG-SYS-04.title: Message title and body length limits
PM-REG-SYS-04.description: Checks that a system message cannot be longer than 2000 characters in the body or 120 in the title.
steps: In the new message form type 2001 characters in the body and 121 in the title.
Click 'Cancel'.
expected: The body stops at 2000 characters ('2000/2000') and the title at 120.
The form closes and nothing is created.

PM-REG-SYS-05.title: Message end date before start date
PM-REG-SYS-05.description: Checks that a system message whose end is earlier than its start is refused with a clear message to the user.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages', click 'New message', enter a test title and a body, set Ends earlier than Starts and click 'Create'.
expected: The message is not created and an error or warning is shown.
PM-REG-SYS-05.actual: The message was not created, but no error or warning was shown. Recorded as defect SCP-DEF-059.

PM-REG-SYS-06.title: Editing a message shows its current content
PM-REG-SYS-06.description: Checks that opening a system message for editing shows its saved title and body, so the user edits the right content.
steps: On System Messages click 'Edit' on the first message (do not click 'Save').
Compare the form with the message in the list.
Click 'Cancel'.
expected: The edit form opens with a 'Save' button.
The title and body are filled in, the counter shows the body length out of 2000 and the preview shows the start of the body.
The form closes and nothing is saved.

PM-REG-SYS-07.title: Create a scheduled system message
PM-REG-SYS-07.description: Checks that a system message set to start in the future is created and shown as scheduled.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Click 'New message', enter a test title, choose Info, set it to start in 7 days and end in 8 days, and click 'Create'.
expected: The page opens.
The message is created and its row shows 'Scheduled'.

PM-REG-SYS-08.title: Active system message shows a banner
PM-REG-SYS-08.description: Checks that a system message active now is shown to users as a banner.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Click 'New message', enter a test title, choose Info, set it from 1 hour ago until tomorrow and click 'Create'.
Reload the page.
expected: The page opens.
The message is created.
A 'Project notice' banner shows the message title and body.

PM-REG-SYS-09.title: Inactive and expired messages show no banner
PM-REG-SYS-09.description: Checks that messages that are switched off or whose time window has passed are not shown to users.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Create one test message with 'Active' unticked and one with a time window in the past, then reload.
Look at the banners on the page.
expected: The page opens.
Both messages are created.
No banner is shown for either message.

PM-REG-SYS-10.title: Delete the run's system messages
PM-REG-SYS-10.description: Checks that system messages can be deleted, so no test banner is left for users.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Delete the run's active test message (accept any confirmation) and reload.
Delete the run's Warning test message and reload.
Delete the run's scheduled test message and reload.
Delete the run's inactive test message and reload.
Delete the run's past test message and reload.
Switch off any message that could not be deleted, then reload.
expected: The page opens.
The result is recorded.
The result is recorded.
The result is recorded.
The result is recorded.
The result is recorded.
No banner from this run is left and every delete worked.

PM-REG-SYS-11.title: Dismiss a message banner
PM-REG-SYS-11.description: Checks that a user can close a message banner and records whether it stays closed after a reload.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
On the run's active 'Project notice' banner click 'Dismiss ×'.
Reload the page.
expected: The page opens.
The banner disappears.
Whether the banner stays hidden is recorded.
PM-REG-SYS-11.actual: As expected. The banner stayed hidden after the reload.

PM-REG-SYS-12.title: Warning and Info banners look different
PM-REG-SYS-12.description: Checks that a Warning message is shown in a different colour from an Info message so users can tell them apart.
steps: Open Project Management > 'System Messages'.
Create a test message with severity 'Warning' that is active now, then reload.
Compare the Warning banner with the Info banner.
expected: The page opens.
The message is created.
The Warning banner has a different background colour from the Info banner.
PM-REG-SYS-12.actual: As expected. The Info banner is light blue and the Warning banner is light yellow.

PM-REG-WM-01.title: Watched Materials prompt before choosing a user
PM-REG-WM-01.description: Checks that Watched Materials asks the user to pick a person before showing any watches.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
Read the page before choosing a user.
expected: The page opens.
The prompt 'Pick a user to view or assign watches.' is shown.

PM-REG-WM-02.title: View a user's watched materials
PM-REG-WM-02.description: Checks that choosing a user shows their watches with type, status and a remove option.
steps: On Watched Materials, pick the signed-in user (or the first real user) in the user dropdown.
Read the watch rows.
expected: The user's watches load.
Each row has a type of 'Category' or 'Trade', a status of On or Off, and a 'Remove' action.

PM-REG-WM-03.title: Watch type and value choices
PM-REG-WM-03.description: Checks that a new watch can be set on a category or trade and that the value list holds the material categories.
steps: On Watched Materials, open the add-watch dropdowns.
expected: The type choices are 'Category' and 'Trade'; the value list holds material categories, matching the Material Category list.

PM-REG-WM-04.title: Watch a material category
PM-REG-WM-04.description: Checks that a user can add a watch on a material category.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
Select the signed-in user in the first dropdown.
Choose 'Category' in the second dropdown and the test category in the third, then click 'Add watch'.
expected: The page opens.
That user's watches are shown.
A watch row of type 'Category' appears.

PM-REG-WM-05.title: Watched category appears on the dashboard
PM-REG-WM-05.description: Checks that a watched category is shown to the user on the Management Dashboard.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
Open 'Management Dashboard' from the left menu and look at 'Your watched materials'.
expected: The page opens.
The test category is listed.

PM-REG-WM-06.title: Same category cannot be watched twice
PM-REG-WM-06.description: Checks that a user cannot add a second watch on a category they already watch.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
Try to add a watch again on the test category that is already watched.
expected: The page opens.
Only one row exists for that category.
PM-REG-WM-06.actual: As expected. The category is no longer offered in the list once it is watched.

PM-REG-WM-07.title: Turn watch notifications off and on
PM-REG-WM-07.description: Checks that a user can switch notifications for a watch off and on, and that the choice is kept after reloading.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
On the test category's row, click the notification button to change it from 'On' to Muted or Off, then reload and select the user again.
Click the notification button until it shows 'On', then reload.
expected: The page opens.
The row shows 'Off' or 'Muted'.

PM-REG-WM-08.description: Checks that removing a watch takes it off both Watched Materials and the Management Dashboard.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
For the signed-in user, click 'Remove' on the test category's row and confirm.
Open 'Management Dashboard' and look at 'Your watched materials'.
On Watched Materials, remove and confirm every remaining watch on test categories created by test runs.
expected: The page opens.
The row is removed.
The test category is no longer listed.
No test category watches are left.

PM-REG-WM-09.title: Watch a trade
PM-REG-WM-09.description: Checks that a user can add a watch on a trade.

Choose 'Trade' in the second dropdown and the first trade, then click 'Add watch'.
expected: The page opens.
A watch row of type 'Trade' appears (this step is skipped when no trades exist).
PM-REG-WM-09.actual: As expected. No trades are set up in project NRVC_Hall, so there was nothing to watch.

PM-REG-WM-10.title: One user can watch every category
PM-REG-WM-10.description: Checks that a single user can watch all material categories, each listed once.
steps: Open Project Management > 'Watched Materials'.
Choose 'Category' and add a watch for every category not yet watched.
Check the watch rows of type 'Category'.
expected: The page opens.

PMD-SETUP.title: Sign in for Project Management tests
PMD-SETUP.description: Checks that the tester can sign in before the Project Management tests start.
steps: Sign in to SCP.

ROLE-SETUP.title: Read each test account's role access
ROLE-SETUP.description: Checks and records what each test account's role allows, without changing anything, as the reference for the role checks.
steps: As Project Admin, read the left menu.
Sign in as the Supplier account in a separate browser.
Sign in as the Subcontractor account in a separate browser.
In Voyage Control Admin > 'Supply Chain Planner' > Roles, open each account's role and read the ticked permissions, then close without saving.
expected: The full list of menu entries is recorded.
SCP opens on NRVC_Hall and the Project Role is read.
SCP opens on NRVC_Hall and the Project Role is read.
The enabled permissions of each role are recorded.

ROLEW-RESTORE.title: Restore the test role and Supplier account
ROLEW-RESTORE.description: Checks that the test role and the Supplier account are put back as they were after the role checks.
steps: Set the test role back to its starting permissions.
Put the Supplier account back on its original Project Role and check it from its own session.
expected: The test role matches its starting permissions.
The Supplier account has its original role.

ROLEW-SETUP.title: Open admin portal and read test role
ROLEW-SETUP.description: Checks that the admin portal opens and records the test role's starting permissions, so they can be restored after the role checks.
steps: Sign in, open Voyage Control Admin > 'Supply Chain Planner' and read the test role.
expected: The test role's starting permissions are recorded.
ROLEW-SETUP.actual: As expected. The test role had 87 permissions.

SHP-REG-01.title: Log a shipment without filling in the form
SHP-REG-01.description: Checks that a shipment cannot be logged with an empty form, so incomplete shipments are not saved.
steps: Open Enterprise > Enterprise Shipments and click '+ Log Shipment'. Check that the Submittal list cannot be used until a Project is chosen, then click 'Log shipment' without filling anything in.
expected: The Submittal list stays disabled until a Project is chosen. The dialog stays open and no 'Shipment logged' message appears.
SHP-REG-01.actual: As expected. The form showed the prompt '— Choose a project —'.

SHP-REG-02.title: Log a shipment for the run's submittal
SHP-REG-02.description: Checks that a user can log an international shipment for a submittal and then find it in the shipments list.
steps: Open Enterprise Shipments and click '+ Log Shipment'. Choose project NRVC_Hall and the run's latest test submittal, enter a manufacturer name, Manufacturer country 'South Korea', a container number, Port of origin 'Busan' and Port of destination 'Chennai', then click 'Log shipment'.
Reopen Enterprise Shipments.
expected: The message 'Shipment logged.' appears.
A row for the logged submittal is listed.
SHP-REG-02.actual: As expected. The shipment row was listed for the run's test submittal.

SHP-REG-03.title: New shipment status follows procurement
SHP-REG-03.description: Checks that a newly logged shipment starts with a status that matches the submittal's procurement progress.
steps: In Enterprise Shipments, read the Status of the logged shipment's row (its submittal is already being delivered).
expected: The status is not 'Pending Order'.
SHP-REG-03.actual: The new shipment's status was 'Pending Order' although its submittal is already being delivered. Recorded as defect SCP-DEF-067.

SHP-REG-04.title: Edit shipping details of a shipment
SHP-REG-04.description: Checks that the shipping line of a logged shipment can be changed and is shown in the list afterwards.
steps: In Enterprise Shipments, click 'Edit' on the shipment row, open 'Edit shipping details', enter a Shipping line name and click 'Save'. Then reopen the list.
expected: The message 'Shipping details updated.' appears and the new name is shown in the 'Shipping Line' column.

SHP-REG-05.title: Shipment status change is kept
SHP-REG-05.description: Checks that changing a shipment's status to 'In Transit' is saved and reflected in the counters and in Enterprise Shipments.
steps: Open International Shipments, note the 'In Transit' tile count, and set the logged shipment's status to 'In Transit'.
Read any confirmation message shown after the change.
Reopen International Shipments.
